content_voiceover: This slide, sourced from Blincyto's own marketing material, shows the mature survival results from that E1910 consolidation trial in MRD negative B-ALL. The primary endpoint was three year overall survival, eighty four point eight percent in the blinatumomab arm of one hundred twelve patients versus sixty nine percent in the chemotherapy only arm of one hundred twelve patients, a hazard ratio of point four two with a p value of point zero zero three, meaning blinatumomab consolidation nearly halved the risk of death. With longer follow up, median three point six years, the benefit persisted and even grew, five year overall survival was eighty two point four percent with blinatumomab compared to just sixty two point five percent with chemotherapy alone, hazard ratio point four four. Looking at the Kaplan-Meier curve, the two arms separate early around year two and the gap widens and holds through year seven of follow up. Notably, MRD negativity in this trial was defined as less than point zero one percent leukemic cells by six color flow cytometry. For boards, this is the practice changing result, in adults with Ph negative B-ALL who achieve MRD negative complete remission, adding blinatumomab to consolidation chemotherapy improves both three year and five year overall survival substantially compared to chemotherapy alone.
keypoints: MRD-negative defined as <0.01% by 6-color flow cytometry
Practice-changing: blina consolidation improves OS in MRD-neg B-ALL
keypoint_voiceover: The bottom line from E1910: adding blinatumomab to consolidation in MRD negative B-ALL nearly halved mortality risk, with five year overall survival of eighty two percent versus sixty three percent for chemotherapy alone, this is the evidence behind blinatumomab's newest consolidation indication.
